original_question: Describe the qualitative properties of spatially non-constant steady states in the landscape-mark memory model, compare them with those of the simpler nonlocal multispecies perception model, and determine whether introducing an explicit cognitive-map variable creates genuinely new dynamics.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2.2, Open Problem 8, for the explicit landscape-mark model (2.11), with Open Problem 7 supplying the steady-state setting and model (2.10) supplying the comparison class. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core intent very well: it asks about qualitative properties of spatially non-constant steady states for the explicit landscape-mark model (2.11), compares them with the simpler multispecies nonlocal perception model (2.10), and asks whether explicitly introducing the extra map/mark variable produces genuinely new dynamics. That is essentially Open Problem 8, almost point for point. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
missing_details: It does not identify the exact target as Open Problem 8 in Section 2.2.2, so it could be confused with nearby but different questions such as Open Problems 7, 10, 12, 18, or 19. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the actual PDE for the target model (2.11): for i = 1, ..., n, ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - γ_i ∇·(u_i ∇p_i^{g,R}) and ∂_t p_i = Σ_{j=1}^n α_{ij} u_j - μ p_i. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
It omits the comparison PDE (2.10): ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - ∇·(u_i ∇(Σ_{j=1}^n γ_{ij} u_j^{g,R})). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the meaning of the variables: u_i is the density of population i, while p_i is the density of foreign marks left on the landscape by other populations. The paper explicitly notes that this memory is stored in the environment rather than in the animal's brain. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the hidden assumptions inherited from the nearby context: a bounded domain, periodic boundary conditions, and a top-hat detection function. These are stated in Open Problem 7 and the surrounding setup for (2.11). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the perception notation f^{g,R}(x) = ∫_Omega f(y) g_R(x-y) dy and the role of the perceptual range R and top-hat kernel g_R. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the parameter list n, d_i, γ_i, α_{ij}, and μ, which are part of the model definition and therefore needed for a stand-alone formulation. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the existential qualifier whenever they exist, which is essential because Open Problem 8 presupposes the existence of spatially non-constant steady states from the preceding Open Problem 7. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It does not state the paper's exact comparison question in its sharpest form: whether the dynamics of model (2.11) are included in the dynamics of model (2.10). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
refined_question: Let Omega be a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions, let g_R be the top-hat detection kernel of perceptual range R, and write f^{g,R}(x) = ∫_Omega f(y) g_R(x-y) dy. For n interacting populations u_i(x,t), consider the explicit landscape-mark model ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - γ_i ∇·(u_i ∇p_i^{g,R}), ∂_t p_i = Σ_{j=1}^n α_{ij} u_j - μ p_i, where p_i is the density of foreign marks left on the landscape. Assuming spatially non-constant steady states of this system exist, what qualitative characteristics can such steady states exhibit, how do they compare with the spatially non-constant steady states of the simpler multispecies nonlocal perception model ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - ∇·(u_i ∇(Σ_{j=1}^n γ_{ij} u_j^{g,R})), and are the dynamics of the explicit landscape-mark model entirely contained in those of the simpler model, or does the explicit mark variable p_i generate genuinely new dynamics? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Are the dynamics of model (2.11) included in the dynamics of model (2.10), or does explicitly introducing the landscape-mark variable lead to new dynamics? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
justification: This is the closest official formulation because Open Problem 8 asks, almost verbatim, for the qualitative characteristics of spatially non-constant steady states of model (2.11), comparison with steady states of model (2.10), and whether increasing complexity via explicit description of the cognitive map yields new dynamics. Open Problem 7 supplies the hidden hypotheses needed to make that question stand alone: the steady-state setting, periodic boundary conditions, bounded domain, and top-hat detection kernel. The nearby definitions of (2.10), (2.11), and the perception operator in Section 2.1 supply the notation and parameters. This is narrower and more faithful than shifting to the later conflict-zone model (2.13), which is a different open problem. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
